summary: Standard chess vs Stockfish with neutral Archangel Gabriel (Mandela Catalogue) on b4. After both White and Black move, every piece adjacent to Gabriel is turned into an 'alternate': a piece controlled by no one that makes its own random move every round (and can capture anything). Gabriel moves one square in a random orthogonal direction each round and cannot capture (blocked by occupied squares). Turn order: White, Black, Gabriel, then all alternates. Narrator sacrifices pawns to create alternates that herd Gabriel into Black's camp, converts enemy pieces (incl. queen) and wins.
rules: Standard chess otherwise; player White vs Stockfish (3600).

Neutral Gabriel starts on b4; each round he moves one square in a random ORTHOGONAL direction to an empty square (cannot capture; if all orthogonal squares are occupied he can't move / is forced to the only empty one).
After White and Black have both moved, every piece on a square adjacent (8 neighbours) to Gabriel becomes an alternate.

Alternates are neutral: neither player controls them; after Gabriel moves, every alternate makes one random legal move in its original movement pattern (pawns keep original direction), and may capture any piece of either colour.
Turn order each round: White, Black, Gabriel, then each alternate.
Kings becoming alternates / captured by alternates: capture of king ends game [inferred].
